title: The Postcard of Maple Hollow
premise: Edmund Underhill inherited Maple Hollow Vineyard along with a mountain of debt and a reputation for failure, while his old rival, winemaker Delia Marsh, returns to town as the consultant hired by the bank that owns his loans. A freak snowstorm traps them in the vineyard's crumbling cellar house with Theo Vance—the charming third member of their college triangle whose testimony once destroyed Edmund's first career—and forces the three to confront the betrayal that scattered their lives a decade ago. As the storm cuts them off from lawyers, banks, and excuses, Edmund and Delia uncover proof that Theo falsified records to save himself, evidence that could clear Edmund but ruin the career Delia has just rebuilt. In the end, they choose each other over safety: they expose the truth at the cost of Delia's position, Edmund wins back the vineyard through the community Theo's fraud had cheated, and the two plant a new season together on ground finally their own.
about_author: Juniper Blackwood is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent seven years working harvests in cold-climate vineyards before turning to fiction. She writes romance about people who mistake survival for living, and she still can't resist a snowbound setting.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He surveys the frozen vineyard he inherited—dead vines, unpaid loans, a foreclosure notice—and reflects on how second chances always arrive too late for people like him. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking grief.

chapters.title: The Consultant Arrives
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. She steps off the bus into Maple Hollow as the bank's hired assessor, stunned to learn the failing property belongs to Edmund Underhill, the man she hasn't spoken to since college. Emotional beat: dread braided with an ache she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Terms of Inspection
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund and Delia conduct a brittle walkthrough of the cellar house, trading barbed professionalism while old memories surface in every barrel room. Emotional beat: antagonism as armor against tenderness.

chapters.title: Theo's Invitation
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Theo Vance sweeps into town as the bank's celebrated regional director, all charm and reconciliation, proposing a dinner to 'settle old history.' Edmund notices Delia flinch. Emotional beat: unease beneath forced civility.

chapters.title: What Happened in the Twenties
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Over wine, Theo retells the scandal that ended Edmund's first career—falsified lab reports, a ruined internship—as if it were harmless anecdote. Delia remembers details that never fit. Emotional beat: the first crack of doubt about the official story.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The forecast turns lethal; roads close; the power fails. The three are stranded together in the cellar house with generator light, dwindling firewood, and ten years of unfinished sentences. Emotional beat: claustrophobic anticipation.

chapters.title: Snowbound Confessions
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Trapped by the blizzard, Delia admits she took the bank job because her own career collapsed after she defended Edmund years ago. He learns, for the first time, what his disgrace cost her. Emotional beat: guilt softening into intimacy.

chapters.title: The Cellar Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Searching for firewood records, Edmund finds his uncle's old ledgers showing shipments that match numbers Theo once cited as 'proof' of fraud. The arithmetic doesn't add up—unless someone altered it. Emotional beat: dawning, dangerous hope.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Fire
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. A near-kiss interrupted by Theo's arrival; Delia pulls back, terrified of wanting something she might have to destroy to survive. Emotional beat: longing at war with self-preservation.

chapters.title: Theo's Version
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone with Edmund, Theo offers a deal: sign the vineyard over quietly and the bank will 'lose' the discrepancies in his file. His charm slips, revealing the ambition underneath. Emotional beat: menace wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund declines the deal, choosing truth over rescue even if it means losing everything again. He tells Delia nothing yet, protecting her from complicity. Emotional beat: quiet, costly courage.

chapters.title: Reading Between Vintages
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia independently cross-checks the ledgers against archived trade journals by lamplight and confirms the forgery pattern—Theo's handwriting habits, unchanged since college. Emotional beat: sickening certainty.

chapters.title: The Night They Stop Pretending
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With the storm at its worst, Edmund and Delia finally speak plainly—about the betrayal, the wasted decade, the almosts—and cross the line they've been circling. Emotional beat: surrender, tender and terrified.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Roads reopen; reality returns with the plows. Delia realizes helping Edmund means torching her own reinstated career and testifying against the man who controls her references. Emotional beat: love colliding with the price of survival.

chapters.title: Theo Tightens the Screws
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sensing exposure, Theo accelerates the foreclosure and hints to the bank that Delia's 'objectivity' is compromised. Power corrupting in real time. Emotional beat: cold triumph curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: Allies in the Hollow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund shares the evidence with townsfolk Theo's fraud also cheated—the co-op farmers, the retired accountant who kept duplicates. Justice outside the law begins assembling itself. Emotional beat: solidarity rising from shared injury.

chapters.title: Delia's Choice
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia drafts her resignation letter and her sworn statement, understanding she may lose the profession that saved her. She signs anyway. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, hands shaking.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the bank's emergency review, Theo performs flawlessly until the duplicated ledgers, the accountant's testimony, and Delia's statement dismantle him piece by piece. Emotional beat: public reckoning, breath-held tension.

chapters.title: Fallen Director
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Exposed and abandoned by the institution he served, Theo faces investigation and tries one last manipulation on Edmund—who offers him not revenge but accountability. Emotional beat: pity where hatred should be.

chapters.title: What the Bank Cannot Own
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With the fraud voided, the community pools resources to buy the vineyard's debt outright, making Maple Hollow a cooperative with Edmund as steward. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: First Pruning
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia, unemployed by choice and lighter for it, stays through the thaw. She and Edmund prune the dead vines together, planning a planting neither could afford alone. Emotional beat: cautious joy taking root.

chapters.title: The Postcard
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. A year later, a postcard arrives at Maple Hollow—a photo of the cellar house under snow, signed by both of them, mailed to no one and everyone: proof that staying invisible was never really an option. Emotional beat: full-circle peace, love made ordinary and lasting.
